result.summary: Adds manual pruning and block-storage flushing functions to the libbitcoinkernel C API, allowing kernel consumers to open pruned datadirs and prune block storage up to a target height. Refactors prune calculation and file-deletion bookkeeping into BlockManager so block storage operations can execute independently of chainstate flushes, and ensures blocks above the fork point between the last flushed block and the active chain are preserved for reorg recovery.
result.problem: Applications using libbitcoinkernel cannot open datadirs created by pruned Bitcoin Core nodes and have no mechanism to prune blocks. Block storage writes and prune tracking were also tightly coupled to FlushStateToDisk in validation.
evidence: Part of #35627: 'kernel: can't work with pruned blocksdir'
Author's description: 'The kernel can't open a data directory that a pruned node created, and it has no way to prune.'
result.scope_notes: Stacked on top of #36738 and #36854; includes multiple internal refactors moving prune locks, limits, and file deletion out of FlushStateToDisk and into BlockManager before exposing the C API surface.
result.card: Adds manual pruning and chainstate flushing functions to the libbitcoinkernel C API (btck_block_manager_prune_up_to_height and btck_chainstate_manager_flush) and enables kernel consumers to open pruned datadirs. Currently, external applications embedding the kernel cannot operate on pruned datadirs or trigger pruning on their own (issue #35627). The underlying block-file deletion logic and prune bookkeeping are extracted from validation's FlushStateToDisk into BlockManager, while ensuring blocks needed for crash recovery during reorgs are retained. This PR is based on #36738 and #36854.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in the prompt, so validation is based solely on commit messages and description.

risk.why: Mistakes in calculating pruning boundaries or deleting block files could discard blocks needed to recover from an unclean shutdown or chain reorg, leading to unrecoverable chainstate corruption.
